# CUTANEOUS ABSCESS

Incise and drain then cover the site with a dry dressing. For small abscesses, systemic antimicrobial therapy is rarely necessary. If the patient is neutropenic, has multiple lesions, or has fever or leukocytosis, antimicrobial treatment may be necessary.

Contact Infectious Diseases for assistance.

## For the few CUTANEOUS ABSCESSES away from the rectal area that need a systemic antimicrobial
Duration: Treat for 5 to 7 days

## Mild to Moderate Cases:

## Moderate or high suspicion of MRSA

Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q12h ($) [R,DI]
< OR >

< OR >

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### For SEVERE cases empiric coverage with MRSA agent

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

### For Perirectal/Anorectal Abscess Select Below

[Perianal/Anorectal Abscess](perianal-anorectal-abscess)

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
Doxycycline 100MG PO Q12H
Clindamycin 300 mg PO q6h ($) [H,O]
Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h ($) [R]
Dicloxacillin 500 mg PO q6h ($) [DI]

## Outpatient

Duration: Treat for 5 to 7 days

### Mild to Moderate Cases:

### Moderate or high suspicion of MRSA

Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid ($) [R,DI]
Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days ($) [DI]

Clindamycin 300 mg po qid for 7 days ($) [H]
### Low suspicion of MRSA

### For SEVERE cases empiric coverage with MRSA agent

See Inpatient CDSS for intravenous therapy

### For Perirectal/Anorectal Abscess Select Below

Perianal/Anorectal Abscess

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Outpatient):*
Cephalexin 500 mg PO qid for 7 days ($) [R]
Dicloxacillin 500 mg PO qid for 7 days ($) [DI]

## ER/UC

Duration: Treat for 5 to 7 days

### Mild to Moderate Cases:

### Moderate or high suspicion of MRSA

Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid ($) [R,DI] for 7 days
Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days ($) [DI]

### Low suspicion of MRSA

### For SEVERE cases empiric coverage with MRSA agent

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV STAT ($) [R]
